ordered_diagnoses: Infectious mononucleosis due to Epstein-Barr virus

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with respiratory and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Painful ecchymotic lesions with hemorrhagic bullae
Multifocal alveolar infiltrates on chest radiography and CT
Thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy on skin biopsy
key_facts: Intermittent night sweats for several months
Arthralgias of the wrists and ankles
Multiple painful ecchymoses with hemorrhagic bullae
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Positive FilmArray respiratory panel for respiratory syncytial virus

shortlist: Infectious mononucleosis due to Epstein-Barr virus

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti-phosphatidylserine IgM

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy showing superficial and deep dermal thrombotic paucicellular vasculopathy

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory and renal involvement, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory symptoms, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and eosinophilic pneumonia possibility

shortlist.label: Henoch-Schönlein purpura
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable purpura, arthralgias, and abdominal involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, weight loss, arthralgias, and multiple painful ecchymoses with hemorrhagic bullae, along with laboratory findings of elevated lactate dehydrogenase, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and positive lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgM, and anti-phosphatidylserine IgM, is most consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis due to Epstein-Barr virus
rejected.why: While the patient has a positive Epstein-Barr virus DNA PCR, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more suggestive of an autoimmune process, such as antiphospholipid syndrome, rather than a viral infection.
